mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates weakening labor market conditions, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate activity (HOUST) signals a weakening demand in the economy, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances when HOUST is declining, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening supply-side conditions, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) and falling real estate activity (HOUST) indicates stagflationary pressures, which reduce corporate earnings and lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month and HOUST falls > 5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises and HOUST falls, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with an increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases > 100k and UNRATE increases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS decreases and UNRATE increases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces borrowing costs and boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS decreases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising retail sales (RSAFS) and falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances when RSAFS increases and UNRATE decreases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
